howTo.title: Register a business with the city
howTo.steps: If you form a corporation, LLC, LP or LLP, register with the state first. Check zoning and pick a location, then complete the Treasurer and Tax Collector's online application, sign the DocuSign email (unsigned applications are deleted after 15 days) and pay the fee. Register within 30 days of starting business in the city; you generally must register if you have a fixed place of business, work in the city for any part of seven days in a year, or rent property for business. Fees for the April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 year run from $55 (gross receipts up to $100,000) to $60,000, plus a $4 state fee. Your Business Account Number is on the payment confirmation; new businesses also file a Business Property Statement (Form 571-L). Renew every year by the end of February.

source.label: SF.gov, Business registration; SF Treasurer and Tax Collector

howTo.title: Put a parklet or outdoor seating in front of your business
howTo.steps: Apply for a Shared Spaces permit through Public Works. As of summer 2026 there is no 10-day public notification period, so you can build right after approval; commercial parklets no longer need public seating but must be open during permitted business hours. Follow the June 2026 design guidelines.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Aug 2026

howTo.title: Get a restaurant liquor license in a priority neighborhood
howTo.steps: California ABC offers nontransferable restaurant licenses for downtown (Union Square and Yerba Buena hospitality zone) and for Bayview, Excelsior, Portola, Ocean Avenue and the Sunset (Type 87). The 2026 priority filing window ran September 14 to 25 with a $19,840 fee; if applications exceed licenses, ABC holds a random drawing, and unsuccessful applicants are refunded less a service charge.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Sep 2026

howTo.title: Make your storefront accessible
howTo.steps: Apply for OEWD's Accessible Barrier Removal Grant, which reimburses up to $10,000 for physical changes such as power door openers, accessible counters and restroom remodels at storefronts in commercially zoned areas.

howTo.title: Get free help in person
howTo.steps: Drop in to an Office of Small Business community office hours session (no appointment) for help with registration, licenses, permits, leasing and funding, or email sfosb@sfgov.org.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Oct 6, 2026

howTo.title: Renew, or remove, a parklet
howTo.steps: Shared Spaces parklet renewals are due November 15, 2026: email an updated Certificate of Insurance and, if it applies, a Neighboring Letter of Consent to SharedSpacesPermit@sfdpw.org. Parklet fees appear on the 2027 Unified License Bill; businesses with gross receipts of $5 million or less a year get a 50 percent waiver automatically. To remove a parklet no removal permit is needed: email a photo of the cleared parking lane with your business name, address and permit number to stop billing.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Nov 2, 2026

howTo.title: Skip first-year city fees for a new business (First Year Free)
howTo.steps: Register the new business or new location with the Treasurer and Tax Collector before you apply for permits; if your San Francisco gross receipts are $5,000,000 or less and the location is commercial, you are enrolled automatically and get an email and letter. Bring them to each permitting agency, which removes the waived fees on the spot. Permits applied for before you register do not qualify. The program runs through June 30, 2027 or until funds run out.

source.label: SF Treasurer and Tax Collector, First Year Free

notices.title: Nov 3 tax measures, preliminary: Muni parcel tax and regional transit sales tax passing
notices.detail: Preliminary results as of 7 am Nov 4 (SF Standard, from Department of Elections data; certification December 3): Proposition H, a parcel tax for Muni, Yes 72.4 percent. For non-residential parcels it is $799 plus $0.76 to $0.99 per square foot of building above 5,000 square feet, capped at $400,000 a parcel, from July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2042, rising with inflation; the SFMTA estimates about $160 million a year. The Regional Transit Measure, a Bay Area sales tax for BART and other transit, Yes 61.5 percent across the region. Proposition J, ending the foreclosure exemption from the real property transfer tax, Yes 79.1 percent. Proposition I, changing the real property transfer tax so half of high-value transfer tax revenue goes to affordable housing, No 55.0 percent.

source.label: SF Standard live results, updated Nov 4, 2026, 7 am

notices.review_note: Preliminary counts; the Department of Elections certifies results December 3. Tax details for Prop H from the official ballot digest (media.api.sf.gov); the $160 million estimate is from the SFMTA's Prop H page.

notices.detail: Send an updated Certificate of Insurance (and a Neighboring Letter of Consent if it applies) to SharedSpacesPermit@sfdpw.org. Parklet fees are on the 2027 Unified License Bill, with an automatic 50 percent waiver for businesses grossing $5 million or less a year.

notices.title: New state laws for businesses, most starting January 1, 2027
notices.detail: The Office of Small Business lists: AB 1693 (a qualified private certifier may approve retail tenant-improvement plans; 20 business days to approve or deny), AB 2418 (private plan check for nonresidential projects when local review would take 30 business days or more), SB 936 and SB 758 (limits on nitrous oxide sales; tobacco sellers may not sell it), AB 1918 (trafficking notices and training at body art facilities), AB 762 (disposable vapes: no import or manufacture from January 1, 2027, no sales from January 1, 2028), SB 1149 (bereavement leave for a designated person) and AB 2663 (restaurant alcohol takeout extended to December 31, 2029).

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Nov 2, 2026

programs.name: Accessible Barrier Removal Grant
programs.what: Reimburses up to $10,000 per business location for accessibility improvements at small business storefronts in commercially zoned areas, such as power door openers, accessible counters and restroom remodels. Rolling applications while funds remain; reopened August 2026.

programs.name: California Paid Family Leave (PFL) Grant
programs.what: State grant for California small businesses of up to $2,000 per employee to offset costs when employees take Paid Family Leave, such as cross-training or hiring temporary staff. No deadline was stated.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Oct 6, 2026

programs.name: Storefront Opportunity Grant
programs.what: Grants of $50,000 to $100,000 for established businesses opening new locations in commercial corridors, to cover first-year costs such as permits, equipment, tenant improvements, deposits and inventory. The Mayor's office said in August 2026 that this grant, Vacant to Vibrant and the Downtown Vibrancy Loan Fund had together helped more than 200 businesses.
programs.review_note: The city page does not say whether applications are currently open.

programs.name: Inner Sunset Neighborhood Vibrancy Grant (SF New Deal)
programs.what: $5,000 to $20,000 for ground-floor storefronts in the Inner Sunset, for beautification, technical assistance or storefront activation. Rolling applications; priority went to those submitted by August 28, 2026.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Aug 2026

programs.review_note: Rolling program; current open status not confirmed after August 2026.

programs.name: OEWD Request for Proposals 237 (deadline November 13)
programs.what: Organizations and businesses can apply to deliver city-funded programs: workforce development and sector training, small business and entrepreneurship support, commercial corridor vitality and activation, arts and cultural economic development, entertainment zones, and organizational development. Applications are due November 13, 2026.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Nov 2, 2026

programs.name: Legacy Business Program and Business Stabilization Grant
programs.what: Recognition, marketing and business help for long-running businesses on the Legacy Business Registry. The Business Stabilization Grant is not taking new applications in fiscal year 2026-27 (July 2026 to June 2027); existing grantees may re-apply. The city also runs a Neighborhood Anchor Business Registry for businesses open 15 years or more.

source.label: Legacy Business Light, Summer/Fall 2026 (Aug 21, 2026); Office of Small Business page

programs.name: First Year Free (permit and license fee waiver)
programs.what: Waives the initial business registration fee, application, inspection and one-time permit fees, and initial license fees (city fees only, not state surcharges) for new businesses or new locations started on or after July 1, 2023 with San Francisco gross receipts of $5,000,000 or less at a commercial location. Home-based businesses and short-term rentals do not qualify. Enrollment is automatic when you register; runs through June 30, 2027 or until the money runs out.

source.label: SF Treasurer and Tax Collector, First Year Free

methodology: Compiled November 4, 2026. Second pass, from pages opened this session: SF.gov's Office of Small Business page and its November (Nov 2) and October 2026 newsletters, Legacy Business Light Summer/Fall 2026, Small Business Commission minutes of Aug 24 and Sept 28, 2026, the qualified ballot measures page, the Prop H ballot digest and the SFMTA's Prop H page, the Treasurer's First Year Free page, a Rec and Park release (Oct 9), the SF Standard (closures tag, Food and Drink, articles of Sept 9 to Nov 4, live results updated Nov 4 at 7 am), SFist (Oct 23), WhatNow (Sept 30), the California EDD September release, Cushman & Wakefield Q3 2026, and the LoopNet and BizBuySell county listing pages. First-pass items are kept. Not found or would not load: the city's grants and loans pages, the Small Business Commission's own page and any October 26 meeting record, Mission Local's restaurant stories, the SF Chronicle (paywalled), and Eater SF and Hoodline (no current stories in searches). The BizBuySell link is the county list's first page; only its second page was opened. Openings listed for November are as announced and marked for review until confirmed.
